breakdown.description: When a specimen is weighed while immersed, buoyancy reduces the apparent weight, so the immersed mass should be smaller than the saturated-in-air mass, not larger.
breakdown.reason: The agent retained the incorrect immersed mass value of 13.6 g instead of correcting it to 8.6 g as in the ground truth. As a result, the agent concluded the data is physically inconsistent, whereas the ground truth (with immersed mass = 8.6 g, which is less than both dry and saturated masses) would lead to the conclusion that the ordering IS physically consistent. The agent identified the physical principle correctly but failed to apply the correction to the numerical value, producing the opposite conclusion from what the ground truth prompt intends.
